headline: AlphaFold-class predictions need biological validation beyond model agreement
label: Alphafold Limits And Applications
summary: Recent benchmarks and genome-scale applications clarify where AlphaFold-class models are reliable and where they mislead.
synthesis: The dominant thread is how far AlphaFold-class predictions can be trusted beyond their nominal accuracy. A benchmark of four folding tools on control, cancer-associated and fusion proteins finds that inter-tool agreement on fusions does not indicate biological plausibility, so consensus alone cannot certify a model. In contrast, AlphaFold models are applied constructively at proteome scale: the AlphaPPM pipeline and MembranomeX resource identify and membrane-orient bitopic proteins across 18 organisms. A separate benchmark of AlphaFold2 and AlphaFold3 on host-pathogen interactions models 6,782 pathogen-human interactions, maps molecular mimicry modes and includes binding-assay validation. The common lesson is that model utility depends on a well-defined target class and external validation. The CoEVFold suite, which visualizes coevolutionary couplings, is adjacent to this theme rather than a direct test of it.
